function: Jointly learns pilot generation, feedback compression of received pilots, and autoencoder encoder and decoder, bypassing explicit channel estimation, to cut CSI acquisition overhead (p. 2; p. 3).
system: Downlink FDD, Mt=32 transmit antennas, single receive antenna, 2 GHz, 10 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 2; p. 4).
method: Deep autoencoder (dense and Conv1D layers) with learned pilots and feedback network, trained end-to-end with categorical cross-entropy (supervised) at 9 dB SNR (p. 3; p. 4).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa channels for the 3GPP 38.901 urban-microcell scenario; 38,400 CSI samples split into 17,920 training, 7,680 validation, 12,800 test (p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained at 9 dB SNR, tested over SNR levels; lp and lf set the network sizes; one QuaDRiGa urban-microcell scenario, split into train, validation, test (p. 3; p. 4).
baselines: Learned: JCF-DAE (joint feedback and DAE, akin to [14]), S-DAE (separate estimation, feedback, DAE, like CEFnet [15]); classical: T-MRT, MRT precoding with reconstructed CSI, 16-QAM (p. 4).
metrics: Symbol error rate versus SNR at 2lp=lf=8 and 16; SER versus pilot and feedback lengths; trainable parameters and FLOPs (p. 3; p. 4; p. 5).
complexity: Table I: trainable parameters and FLOPs of feedback, encoding, and decoding NNs (pilot generation not counted); extra parameters and FLOPs of baseline modules in text (p. 3; p. 4).
openness: none; QuaDRiGa [13] is cited as the simulator, but no code or data link is given (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "is generated using QuaDriGa [13], designed for 3GPP 38.901" - urban-microcell scenarios; the training, validation, and test samples all come from this QuaDRiGa data.
q2_support: p. 4: "samples, divided into training, validation, and test datasets" - a held-out split of the same QuaDRiGa data; training at 9 dB SNR with an SNR sweep, and lp, lf resize the networks (p. 3); no new scenario, band, or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "performance further improves by about 1 dB compared to" JCF-DAE and about 2 dB compared to S-DAE (learned, modeled on [14] and CEFnet [15]), and about 5 dB over the traditional T-MRT precoding.
q4_support: p. 3: "of trainable parameters and floating-point operations (FLOPs)" - Table I gives the parameters and FLOPs of the feedback, encoding, and decoding NNs.
q5_support: p. 4: "We generate a total of 38,400 CSI" samples with QuaDRiGa - the authors' own generated data; no code or data link, public dataset, or measurement is given.
notes: Area 2 because the contribution is CSI acquisition (AI-generated pilots plus feedback compression, p. 1; p. 2); the encoder and decoder also make it a precoding and detection design with SER as main metric, so areas 3 or 1 are possible. q3 borderline: JCF-DAE and S-DAE are reimplementations akin to [14] and CEFnet [15], and T-MRT uses CSI reconstructed by the separate scheme's networks (p. 4).
